subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat plus cron expressions?
rationale: The remaining request changes public scheduling semantics and persisted config shape, and repository policy treats config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve current fixed `everyMs` plus `anchorMs` semantics and rely on heartbeat phase plus cron-expression stagger for anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Add broader prime mode
options.body: Accept a larger product surface for prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls across heartbeat and cron, with migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on cron stagger semantics and the current scheduling/config policy boundary.
